explanation: Always take a drop in baby kicks seriously! It can be a vital warning sign that the baby is under distress and needs an urgent check-up. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T49#GNS214_U1_T49_h5)

question: How does a flannel graph help you out during a community health talk?

options.A: By measuring the blood pressure of clients during community outreaches
options.B: By printing thousands of takeaway leaflets for mothers attending the clinic
options.C: By allowing the nurse to move felt illustrations on a board to tell an interactive story
options.D: By broadcasting recorded audio messages across the entire village square

explanation: Flannel graphs use fuzzy cut-outs that stick to a board. As you talk, you can move them around to build a fun, visual story with your audience! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T5#GNS124_U5_T5_h4)

question: Which vital sign changes usually give us the very first warning that a patient is in distress?

options.A: Elevated blood sugar and sodium
options.B: Increased heart and breathing rates
options.C: Loss of bowel sounds and appetite
options.D: Decreased body temperature and weight

explanation: Great job! When the body feels stressed or short of oxygen, it automatically makes the heart and lungs work faster to compensate, even before blood pressure drops. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T11#GNS123_U5_T11_h2)

question: Which nursing action provides the most accurate daily measurement of fluid retention in a hospitalized patient?

options.A: Asking the patient how tight their shoes feel each morning
options.B: Weighing the patient at the exact same time every day on the same scale
options.C: Measuring the abdominal girth with a soft tape measure once per shift
options.D: Counting how many times the patient asks to use the restroom

explanation: Daily weights using the same scale and clothing weight offer the most reliable data on whether fluid is accumulating or being successfully removed. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h5)

question: What body tissue is the primary driver of a person's metabolic rate?

options.A: Bone mineral matrix
options.B: Subcutaneous water
options.C: Adipose fat tissue
options.D: Lean muscle mass

explanation: Muscle tissue burns significantly more calories at rest than fat tissue, making muscle mass the main driver of metabolism. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h4)

question: Why is it discouraged to use the word 'prove' in a research objective?

options.A: It makes the study take much longer to complete
options.B: A single study gathers evidence to test a hypothesis, rather than proving an absolute truth
options.C: The word 'prove' is grammatically incorrect in scientific writing
options.D: Ethics committees do not allow researchers to have strong opinions

explanation: Science builds knowledge brick by brick. A single study only gathers evidence to support or reject an idea—it rarely claims to 'prove' an absolute truth once and for all. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h7)

question: Which visual chart is most commonly used to map out a project timeline in a research proposal?

options.A: Scatter plot
options.B: Flowchart diagram
options.C: Gantt chart
options.D: Pie chart

explanation: A Gantt chart is a handy bar chart layout that helps you schedule out your project tasks and deadlines across the weeks or months of your study. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T2#GNS224_U3_T2_h9)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended strategy for overcoming MBO barriers in a hospital?

options.A: Celebrating small clinical wins with the nursing team
options.B: Integrating goal tracking into existing routine staff meetings
options.C: Training managers to offer supportive guidance during reviews
options.D: Adding dozens of complex new metrics for every single shift

explanation: Adding excessive metrics increases paperwork and stress, which directly harms MBO implementation. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h7)

question: How do EMR systems help stop medication mistakes compared to old paper charts?

options.A: By eliminating the problem of misreading messy handwriting
options.B: By automatically administering drugs without nurse approval
options.C: By letting patients prescribe their own medication at home
options.D: By completely removing the need for doctors to write orders

explanation: We've all squinted at difficult handwriting! Clear digital text keeps patients safe by taking the guesswork out of doctor's orders. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h1)

question: Why does the VAPP Act break down violence into clear, specific categories like physical, emotional, and economic?

options.A: To exempt family members from legal penalties
options.B: To make it easier for lawyers and judges to properly prosecute offenders
options.C: To reduce the number of reported court cases
options.D: To ensure that only physical injuries receive medical attention

explanation: Spot on! Clear categories remove legal loopholes, making sure every form of mistreatment is properly addressed by the justice system. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T14#GNS312_U4_T14_h3)

question: What is the very first step a nurse must take to become truly culturally competent?

options.A: Insist that patients adopt modern hospital habits
options.B: Abandon all western medical training completely
options.C: Examine their own personal biases and values
options.D: Memorize the medical laws of every country

explanation: Self-reflection is key! Before we can understand others, we have to look inward and recognize our own unique cultural viewpoints and biases. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h5)

question: What does the presence of thick meconium-stained amniotic fluid usually indicate?

options.A: Rapid dilation of the maternal cervix
options.B: A normal and healthy progression of labour
options.C: Normal kidney function in a full-term baby
options.D: Previous foetal stress and bowel relaxation

explanation: Hypoxia relaxes the foetal anal sphincter, causing the baby to pass meconium into the amniotic fluid before delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h3)

question: Why must a nurse check a female patient's surgical history before placing an IV in her arm?

options.A: To confirm she is not currently allergic to standard soap.
options.B: To avoid placing an IV on the same side as a prior mastectomy.
options.C: To make sure she has never received a blood transfusion before.
options.D: To ensure her blood pressure can be measured safely on that arm.

explanation: Lymph node removal during a mastectomy impairs lymphatic drainage, making that arm vulnerable to swelling and severe infection if punctured. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h4)

question: How does home care primarily reduce patient anxiety compared to hospital stays?

options.A: By keeping patients in a familiar environment near loved ones and daily routines
options.B: By guaranteeing that doctors visit the home every single hour
options.C: By stopping family members from visiting during stressful treatment times
options.D: By eliminating the need for any medications or painful procedures

explanation: Familiar surroundings and personal routines help lower stress and confusion for recovering patients. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h2)

question: You notice a post-op fistula patient has stopped draining urine into her catheter bag. What should you check first?

options.A: The surgical repair has already completely healed within two days
options.B: The patient has started drinking too much water too quickly
options.C: The patient's kidneys have permanently stopped working overnight
options.D: The catheter tubing might be blocked with mucus or a blood clot

explanation: Spot on! A sudden stop in urine flow usually means a blockage in the tube that needs your quick assessment and possible flushing. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h5)

question: What is the main job of the endocrine system in our body?

options.A: Defending the body against foreign pathogens
options.B: Regulating body functions through hormone secretion
options.C: Filtering waste products directly from the bloodstream
options.D: Providing structural support for internal organs

explanation: Think of the endocrine system as your body's chemical messaging network! It uses glands to release hormones straight into the blood, controlling everything from growth to metabolism. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T3#GNS222_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is gluten's main job when baking bread and pastries?

options.A: It acts as a primary artificial sweetener
options.B: It preserves food against bacterial spoilage
options.C: It gives dough elasticity and chewy texture
options.D: It adds essential vitamin C to baked goods

explanation: Think of gluten as the stretchy protein network that traps gases, giving bread its lovely bounce and structure! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h1)

question: Which of these is a common traditional widowhood practice that involves keeping a widow away from others?

options.A: Permanent physical exile from the community
options.B: Mandatory immediate relocation to another state
options.C: Confinement in a secluded room for an extended period
options.D: Ban on speaking to any male healthcare worker

explanation: Many traditions require a grieving widow to stay locked away from public view for weeks or months as part of the mourning customs. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T10#GNS225_U6_T10_h2)

question: You are getting instruments ready for a deep abdominal surgery. How must these tools be processed?

options.A: Low-level disinfection
options.B: Sterilization
options.C: High-level disinfection
options.D: Thorough soap washing

explanation: Any tool going into sterile body tissue or blood vessels is a critical item and absolutely must be sterilized! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the most important instruction to give a patient taking a multi-day course of antifungal pills?

options.A: Stop taking the pills immediately as soon as itching stops
options.B: Save half the medication in case the infection returns next month
options.C: Double the dose on the final day to clear out remaining yeast
options.D: Finish the entire prescription even if symptoms go away completely

explanation: Even if the itching stops, a few sneaky fungi might still be alive. Always finish the full dose to keep the infection from bouncing back! [learn more](GNS223_U8_T3#GNS223_U8_T3_h6)

question: As student nurses, we always hear about confidentiality. What does it actually mean?

options.A: Documenting all personal feelings in public charts
options.B: Keeping patient information private and secure
options.C: Sharing patient stories with the entire clinic staff
options.D: Telling family members everything the patient says

explanation: Confidentiality means what happens in the counselling session stays between you and the patient. Trust is everything! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h3)

question: What is a very common challenge that stops clinical nurses from using research on busy shifts?

options.A: Lack of time during busy hospital shifts
options.B: An excess of research journals in the breakroom
options.C: Mandatory daily research exams for all staff
options.D: Too much free time available on the ward

explanation: True! Heavy workloads and packed hospital shifts mean nurses often struggle to find free time to sit down and read research papers. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T4#GNS217_U2_T4_h8)

question: What is the main goal of a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) after something goes wrong in the hospital?

options.A: Calculating the financial cost of lost equipment
options.B: Finding a junior nurse to blame and dismissing them immediately
options.C: Hiding the incident from the hospital management board
options.D: Discovering underlying system flaws that allowed the error to happen

explanation: RCA doesn't look for someone to point a finger at; it digs deep into the system to fix broken processes so it never happens again. [learn more](GST321_U1_T2#GST321_U1_T2_h8)

question: Why do adolescent girls need extra iron in their diet?

options.A: To build stronger heart valves
options.B: To compensate for menstrual blood loss
options.C: To accelerate the growth of facial hair
options.D: To prevent the softening of tooth enamel

explanation: Correct! Because of monthly periods, girls lose some iron and need a good diet to keep their blood healthy and prevent anemia. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h7)

question: In public health, what does 'host resistance' mean?

options.A: The physical barrier created by wearing heavy protective clothing
options.B: The ability of an infectious agent to survive inside a harsh environment
options.C: The total of all natural and acquired defenses that protect against infection
options.D: The rate at which a community spreads a contagious virus

explanation: Host resistance is your body's shield—all your natural and built-up defenses working together to keep germs out and stop infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T79#GNS214_U1_T79_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse should do when dealing with harmful traditional practices?

options.A: Performing the harmful traditional practice to please community elders
options.B: Offering supportive counseling to women resisting the practice
options.C: Providing respectful health education on the dangers involved
options.D: Reporting illegal procedures or child abuse to the right authorities

explanation: As a nurse, your first loyalty is to your patient's safety. You should never take part in harmful traditional practices, no matter the local pressure! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h8)

question: A hospitalized patient has a very low prealbumin level and a very high C-reactive protein (CRP). How should you read these results?

options.A: The low prealbumin is likely caused by inflammation rather than pure starvation.
options.B: The lab results cancel each other out and provide no useful clinical data.
options.C: The high CRP proves the patient is absorbing all dietary proteins properly.
options.D: The patient definitely needs an emergency tube feeding for protein deficiency.

explanation: Spotting inflammation (via high CRP) helps you realize that low protein levels might be due to the illness itself, not just poor eating. Clinical puzzle solved! [learn more](GNS227_U5_T005#GNS227_U5_T005_h5)

question: You touch a hot pot in the clinical kitchen and instantly pull your hand back. Which fibers carried the signal from your CNS out to your hand muscles?

options.A: Sensory fibers
options.B: Efferent fibers
options.C: Receptor fibers
options.D: Afferent fibers

explanation: E-fferent exits the brain with instructions (think 'E' for exit). Quick reflexes keep future nurses safe! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h4)

question: When is a syringe driver most likely to be used for a patient?

options.A: When the patient refuses all forms of nursing care
options.B: When intravenous access is completely forbidden by law
options.C: When the patient needs rapid blood pressure support
options.D: When oral medications are no longer safe or possible

explanation: Exactly! If a patient cannot swallow, has severe vomiting, or is nearing the end of life, a syringe driver is a lifesaver for giving regular medications smoothly. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h2)

question: Why is following a strict code of ethics so important for a nurse?

options.A: It ensures the nurse receives the highest possible salary tier
options.B: It eliminates the need for any formal continuing education classes
options.C: It guarantees patient confidentiality, dignity, and fairness in care
options.D: It grants the nurse legal authority to perform major surgeries

explanation: Our ethical code is our compass. It guides us to treat every patient fairly, keep their secrets safe, and always respect their human dignity. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the typical average length of a complete ovarian cycle?

options.A: 28 days
options.B: 40 days
options.C: 14 days
options.D: 7 days

explanation: A standard text-book ovarian cycle is calculated to last about twenty-eight days, though normal variations among women are very common. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of competitive bidding when buying DRF supplies?

options.A: To delay the purchasing process until more patients arrive
options.B: To ensure only foreign pharmaceutical companies win contracts
options.C: To secure the best quality drugs at fair and reasonable prices
options.D: To eliminate the need for physical stock verification checks

explanation: Asking multiple suppliers to bid gives the hospital choices, ensuring you get top-quality medicines without getting overcharged. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T3#GNS215_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the paired paranasal sinuses?

options.A: Maxillary sinus
options.B: Frontal sinus
options.C: Temporal sinus
options.D: Sphenoid sinus

explanation: The temporal bone does not contain a paranasal sinus; the four paired sinuses are maxillary, frontal, sphenoid, and ethmoid. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h4)

question: What do we call the exercise where the nurse moves the patient's joint for them, without the patient doing any work?

options.A: Active-assisted movement
options.B: Passive range-of-motion exercise
options.C: Isometric muscle contraction
options.D: Resistive weight-training exercise

explanation: Correct! 'Passive' means the patient is relaxed while you do the moving to keep their joints nice and flexible. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h4)

question: Why might a nurse rush to handle a sudden disease outbreak over a common chronic illness?

options.A: The high severity and community panic demand immediate action
options.B: Outbreaks require no financial resources or planning
options.C: Government rules forbid treating long-term conditions
options.D: Chronic illnesses are impossible to treat in communities

explanation: Spot on! Sudden outbreaks spread fast and put lives in immediate danger, so they jump straight to the top of the priority list. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h4)

question: What does a MUAC tape measure during a nutritional assessment?

options.A: Mid-upper arm circumference
options.B: Maximum umbilical abdominal capacity
options.C: Microorganism antibody count
options.D: Monthly urine acidity concentration

explanation: MUAC is your best friend in community pediatrics! It's that colorful tape wrapped around a child's arm to quickly check for severe acute malnutrition. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h4)

question: What does 'deinfibulation' mean when managing FGM complications?

options.A: Routine removal of the ovaries to prevent hormonal imbalances
options.B: A traditional herbal massage used to reduce pelvic inflammation
options.C: The practice of re-sewing the labia tightly after every menstrual cycle
options.D: Surgical opening of the scar tissue seal to restore normal anatomy

explanation: Deinfibulation is simply surgically opening the fused labia (from Type III FGM) so the patient can urinate, menstruate, and give birth safely. Fantastic job learning this! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why is it often harder for instructors to grade a student's affective domain compared to their cognitive knowledge?

options.A: Clinical instructors are not legally allowed to grade student behavior.
options.B: Students never display their true attitudes while in the clinical setting.
options.C: There are no written rules or guidelines for professional nursing behavior.
options.D: Internal feelings and attitudes must be inferred from observable actions rather than direct measurements.

explanation: Since teachers can't read your mind, they watch how you treat patients and colleagues every day to gauge your professional attitude. You're developing great habits! [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h5)

question: How can poor food storage at home harm a child's health?

options.A: It lowers the market price of local vegetables.
options.B: It reduces the child's daily physical activity levels.
options.C: It automatically increases the vitamin content of stored grains.
options.D: It causes foodborne infections that trigger diarrhea and hinder nutrient absorption.

explanation: Spot on! Spoiled or contaminated food leads to tummy infections, making it hard for the child's body to keep the nutrients it needs. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T031#GNS227_U2_T031_h6)

question: What is the primary underlying problem in all types of shock?

options.A: Inadequate tissue perfusion
options.B: Elevated blood glucose levels
options.C: Excessive carbon dioxide retention
options.D: Severe localized tissue trauma

explanation: Shock fundamentally happens when blood flow is insufficient to supply oxygen and nutrients to the body's tissues and organs. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T3#GNS112_U7_T3_h1)

question: Why are metabolic and endocrine disorders considered such a big deal for public health?

options.A: They only affect elderly populations in rural areas
options.B: They are easily cured with a single antibiotic
options.C: They cause widespread and systemic complications
options.D: They never require long-term medical management

explanation: Because our hormones control so many different body systems, when something goes wrong here, it affects the whole body. Great thinking! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h1)

question: What is a major consequence when young girls experience unplanned early pregnancies?

options.A: They receive free healthcare for the rest of their lives
options.B: They gain immediate leadership roles in politics
options.C: They automatically achieve financial independence
options.D: They are frequently forced to drop out of school

explanation: Unplanned early pregnancy is a leading cause of school dropout among young girls, restricting their future employment opportunities. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h4)

question: Why is thin, watery pap discouraged as the main food when starting a baby on solid foods?

options.A: It lacks sufficient energy and nutrients for a growing baby
options.B: It introduces too much protein for immature kidneys
options.C: It makes the infant completely reject breast milk
options.D: It causes immediate choking in infants under six months

explanation: Spot on! Watery pap fills up a baby's tiny tummy with mostly water, leaving very little room for the energy and nutrients they need to grow. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T2#GNS225_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is a major barrier that keeps Nigerian men away from maternal clinics?

options.A: Traditional beliefs that babies bring bad luck
options.B: Long waiting times that conflict with daily work
options.C: Federal laws forbidding men from entering wards
options.D: A complete lack of roads leading to any hospital

explanation: Since many men hustle for daily wages, spending hours waiting at a clinic can hurt their daily survival. Makes total sense! [learn more](GNS312_U4_T7#GNS312_U4_T7_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to client-centered drug administration in hospitals?

options.A: Institutional time pressures during busy medication passes
options.B: Heavy workloads and short nursing staff numbers
options.C: Having too many clinical pharmacists available on every shift
options.D: Language differences between the nurse and the patient

explanation: Having more clinical pharmacists actually helps improve medication safety rather than acting as a barrier to care. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is the main goal of pasteurizing commercial milk?

options.A: To increase the natural sugar and fat percentages
options.B: To destroy all disease-causing pathogens safely
options.C: To remove every single living microbe and spore
options.D: To convert all liquid milk completely into cheese

explanation: You got it! Pasteurization uses heat to knock out harmful germs so the milk is safe to drink, even though it doesn't kill every single spore. [learn more](GST114_U3_T4#GST114_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why do laboratories test for indicator organisms instead of every pathogen?

options.A: Indicator bacteria neutralize all other chemical toxins
options.B: Pathogens cannot survive long enough to be detected in labs
options.C: Testing for every single pathogen is too difficult and expensive
options.D: Indicator organisms are the only microbes that cause illness

explanation: Pathogens are numerous and hard to isolate individually, so checking for reliable indicators is faster and more practical. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which antibody is the main culprit behind fast allergic drug reactions?

options.A: IgA
options.B: IgG
options.C: IgM
options.D: IgE

explanation: Immunoglobulin E (IgE) is the allergy antibody. It sticks to mast cells and sets off a quick release of histamine. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h2)

question: In many communities, which group faces a high risk from improperly disposed medical waste due to scavenging at dump sites?

options.A: Informal waste pickers and scavengers
options.B: Hospital administrative office managers
options.C: Licensed medical equipment vendors
options.D: Senior medical consultants and surgeons

explanation: That's right. People who sort through open municipal dumps to find reusable items often run into discarded needles and toxic waste without any protective gear. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h5)

question: What is a great way institutional kitchens keep food costs under control?

options.A: Serving only imported luxury foods every single day
options.B: Eliminating all vegetables from the daily meal plan
options.C: Ignoring food waste and throwing away leftover ingredients
options.D: Practicing careful portion control and buying in bulk

explanation: Buying in large quantities and serving the right portions helps save money and cuts down waste. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T005#GNS227_U3_T005_h6)

question: At what stage do primary oocytes pause their development while a baby girl is still in the womb?

options.A: Telophase of mitosis
options.B: Anaphase of meiosis II
options.C: Metaphase of meiosis II
options.D: Prophase of meiosis I

explanation: Think of it like hitting a pause button. Primary oocytes pause in prophase of meiosis I before a baby girl is even born, and they stay paused for years! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T9#GNS121_U5_T9_h2)

question: In chronic kidney disease, why do we need to restrict foods that are high in phosphorus?

options.A: To stop the sudden accumulation of excess stomach acid
options.B: To stimulate healthy red blood cell production in the bone marrow
options.C: To reduce the frequency of painful urinary tract infections
options.D: To prevent bone disease and dangerous vascular calcification

explanation: Failing kidneys struggle to clear phosphorus. Excess phosphorus steals calcium from the bones and hardens blood vessels, which spells trouble for the heart. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h4)

question: What is the purpose of drawing an epidemic curve during an investigation?

options.A: To measure the physical distance between infected houses
options.B: To test the purity of local water supplies in a lab
options.C: To visualize how the infection spread over time
options.D: To calculate the total budget spent on patient drugs

explanation: An epidemic curve is a graph that shows the onset of cases over time, helping investigators understand the outbreak's pattern. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h5)

question: How is endocrine signaling different from nervous system signaling?

options.A: Nervous signaling produces much slower, permanent bodily changes
options.B: Nervous signaling relies entirely on circulating blood vessels
options.C: Endocrine signaling uses direct physical contact with cells
options.D: Endocrine signaling is slower and has longer-lasting effects

explanation: Nerve impulses are like a quick flash of lightning, while hormones are like a slow, steady wave whose effects linger much longer. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T4#GNS211_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is a key nursing duty during the disaster preparedness phase?

options.A: Conducting community education and hazard awareness training
options.B: Demolishing unsafe buildings before an earthquake occurs
options.C: Writing national disaster budget legislation
options.D: Importing foreign medical equipment without authorization

explanation: Well done! Getting ready means educating the public so everyone knows what to do before an emergency strikes. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T12#GNS315_U1_T12_h5)

question: What triggers a nurse to place a new order for a medical supply item?

options.A: When the hospital accountant visits the ward for an inspection
options.B: When the stock balance drops down to the reorder level
options.C: When the expiration date of the current batch is reached
options.D: When the storage shelf is completely empty and bare

explanation: The reorder level acts as an early warning system, giving enough time for new supplies to arrive before safety stock is touched. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h3)

question: What is the main role of the parasympathetic nervous system during a quiet meal?

options.A: Dilating the airways for heavy running
options.B: Releasing emergency sugar stores
options.C: Promoting digestion and resting
options.D: Accelerating the heart rate

explanation: The parasympathetic division dominates during quiet, non-stressful times to support digestion and energy conservation. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T29#GNS211_U3_T29_h2)

question: What is the main surgical option used to treat severe stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: Widening the urethral opening with a stent
options.B: Placing a supportive sling under the urethra
options.C: Implanting an artificial kidney to filter urine
options.D: Removing the lower portion of the bladder

explanation: A surgical sling acts like a little hammock or seatbelt underneath the urethra to keep it from dropping when you move. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h7)

question: According to the Health Belief Model, what pushes someone to finally adopt a new health habit?

options.A: Being forced by local law enforcement officers to visit the clinic
options.B: Forgetting that diseases exist in their local environment
options.C: Receiving financial payment for every health clinic visit
options.D: Believing the health threat is serious and the benefits outweigh the barriers

explanation: Exactly! People are ready to make a change when they see a real personal risk and feel that the solution is easy enough to do. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h2)

question: You are assessing a patient with a newly created AV fistula in their arm. What finding tells you it is open and working well?

options.A: A palpable thrill and audible bruit over the fistula site
options.B: Absence of any sound or vibration when listening with a stethoscope
options.C: A cool hand with weak pulses past the surgical site
options.D: A strong pulse with severe pain and redness in the fingers

question: What does the intraarticular route of medication administration involve?

question: Why must nurses emphasize treating sexual partners when a teenager is diagnosed with a bacterial STI?

question: Which nursing diagnosis focuses directly on blood supply to the brain tissue?

question: What is the main purpose of using non-pharmacological comfort measures alongside prescription drugs?

question: In a centralised nursing setup, where are all the major decisions typically made?

question: How do alkylating agents mainly damage cancer cells?

question: How should a nurse best approach diet education for a patient going home with a new health condition?

question: What is a major benefit of connecting a visually impaired patient with a peer support group?

options.A: Diagnosing the underlying cause of their eye disease
options.B: Providing free medical treatments and prescription drugs
options.C: Sharing practical coping strategies and reducing isolation
options.D: Replacing the need for professional nursing home care

question: Which food texture is safest for a patient with severe swallowing difficulties and missing teeth?

options.A: Regular solid
options.B: Raw vegetables

options.D: Mechanically soft

explanation: Pureed foods are smooth and need zero chewing effort, making them much safer and easier for a struggling patient to swallow. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h5)

question: Why are community health nurses in a great position to spot children at risk of delinquency?

options.A: They possess the exclusive legal authority to arrest young lawbreakers
options.B: They interact with families across homes, schools, and clinics regularly
options.C: They spend most of their working hours inside maximum-security prisons
options.D: They are the only healthcare workers trained in psychological diagnosis

explanation: Spot on! Because nurses visit homes, schools, and clinics, they see family dynamics firsthand and can catch early warning signs. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T4#GNS225_U5_T4_h4)

question: A patient takes their normal drug, but after drinking a lot of an enzyme-inhibiting juice, they show signs of drug toxicity. What happened?

question: What role do continuing professional development programs play in nursing?

options.A: They guarantee automatic promotion to hospital director

options.D: They replace the need for initial basic nursing training

question: A patient with mild arthritis struggles to open childproof medicine caps, so they leave bottles wide open on the table. What is the best nursing advice?

question: How often should emergency crash carts and equipment usually be checked?

question: Why does HIV specifically attack CD4+ T-cells and macrophages?

question: A patient with a head injury has a lower Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score than before. What does this usually mean?

options.A: Normal recovery from sedation medication

options.C: Improvement in overall muscle strength

question: What is the big worry with secondary brain injuries after a sudden head trauma or stroke?

options.A: Cellular damage continues to unfold over hours and days after the initial insult.

options.C: Blood pressure drops to zero throughout the entire systemic circulation.

question: What do we call wound drainage that is clear and watery?

question: Which of these is NOT part of a routine check on a new mother's digestive recovery?

question: Why do nurses sometimes easily miss mental health struggles in patients with physical disabilities?

options.A: Psychological assessment is outside the legal scope of nursing

options.C: Physical symptoms like pain and wounds demand immediate attention

question: Why is storing medications inside a steamy bathroom cabinet a bad idea?

options.A: Pill bottles rust quickly when exposed to daily soap bubbles

options.C: Bathrooms lack locks to keep medications away from visitors

explanation: Heat and humidity break down active drug ingredients, making the medicines less effective over time. Cool, dry storage is always best! [learn more](GNS324_U2_T8#GNS324_U2_T8_h4)

question: You hear gurgling sounds and see thick secretions in an unconscious patient's mouth. What is your very first action?

question: Which condition happens when the body makes insulin, but the cells do not respond to it properly (insulin resistance)?

options.A: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.B: Primary lactic acidosis
options.C: Phenylketonuria
options.D: Type 1 diabetes mellitus

question: What is the main goal of using a disinfectant on hospital equipment?

options.A: To reduce pathogenic microorganisms on inanimate surfaces to safe levels

options.C: To kill transient flora on human skin before an injection
options.D: To remove organic matter from surgical instruments

explanation: Disinfection is all about lowering germ counts on objects to a safe level, rather than achieving total sterility. That's why it targets regular germs instead of tough bacterial spores! [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h1)

question: A patient wants to enter an SNF simply because they feel lonely at home and need help cooking meals. Why might this admission be delayed or denied coverage?

options.A: Social workers are not allowed to review home situations
options.B: The patient lacks a need for daily skilled nursing or therapy services
options.C: Medicare covers custodial care for anyone requesting it
options.D: The facility only accepts patients with infectious diseases

explanation: SNF coverage is meant for active medical or therapy needs, rather than basic social support or housekeeping help. Makes total sense! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h3)

question: Giving routine childhood immunizations is an example of which level of prevention?

options.A: Quaternary prevention
options.B: Secondary prevention

question: How do teenagers typically react when adults respond to adolescent mistakes with harsh anger and judgment?

question: What happens when different tiers of government fail to coordinate their healthcare efforts?

question: What marks the biological beginning of the adolescent period?

question: What is the main difference between skilled care and custodial care?

question: What is the main difference between casual drug use and addiction?

question: Which substance is often given early to trap toxins in the stomach before they get into the bloodstream?

question: Which sign tells you a limb with a tight, wrapping (circumferential) burn is developing compartment syndrome?

question: Why is ethical clearance and consent so important even in observational nursing studies?

question: Which of these tasks is usually handled by a nursing assistant rather than a Registered Nurse (RN)?

question: How long should you wash your hands with soap and water before handling food?

question: A young man comes to the clinic with sudden, severe pain in one side of his scrotum, and the testicle appears unusually high. What is the most likely issue?

question: Which patient has the highest risk of developing cholesterol gallstones?

question: Which type of adverse drug reaction is predictable and related to the drug's normal pharmacological action?

question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to protect external validity in clinical research?

question: Why is visiting a patient with psychosis at home so helpful for a nurse?

question: Which ethical principle simply means a nurse or researcher must 'do no harm' to study participants?

question: Which of these is a key focus when assessing a nursing student's affective domain?

question: Which regulatory body sets the professional and legal standards for nursing practice and documentation in Nigeria?

question: Why shouldn't you rely purely on assumptions when planning a new community health program?

question: Where are the descending motor fibers found as they pass through the pons?

question: Your clinic has limited funds and staff. How should you decide which health problem to tackle first?

question: Where in the brain is the main control center for the cough reflex located?

question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to ensure a health project is sustainable?

question: What is the most immediate life-threatening risk right after FGM is performed?

question: What is the main job of an anaerobic chamber in the microbiology lab?

question: What is the primary danger of delaying stock card updates until the end of the week?

question: Which method gives the fastest whole-body delivery of corticosteroids during a serious medical emergency?

question: Why do we apply a cold pack to an insect sting right after it happens?

question: Why do babies with sickle cell anaemia usually look completely healthy at birth?

question: Why do patients with basal ganglia problems sometimes experience changes in mood or behavior?

question: What is the main job of topical corticosteroids in skin care?

options.C: Killing superficial bacterial infections
options.D: Reducing inflammation and immune response

question: What is the primary purpose of monitoring a Behavioural Change Communication program?

question: How does the slow block to polyspermy protect the newly formed zygote?

question: A nursing student observes a mother struggling to latch her newborn baby. What instruction should the nurse give first?

question: Which of these is a must-share piece of information during a patient handover?

options.A: The brand name of the hospital bed mattress
options.B: The patient's favorite television program
options.C: The personal phone number of the patient's relative
options.D: Current vital signs and recent lab results

explanation: Vitals and lab values give a clear, quick picture of how stable the patient is right now. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h4)

question: As a nurse, you'll hear about SBAR. What does this acronym stand for?

options.A: Shift, Bed, Analysis, Report
options.B: System, Blood, Assessment, Reaction
options.C: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.D: Safety, Basic, Action, Review

explanation: Spot on! SBAR is your best friend for quick, clear handovers and phone calls with doctors. It helps you state the Situation, give the Background, share your Assessment, and state your Recommendation. [learn more](GST321_U1_T12#GST321_U1_T12_h2)

question: Why do anticholinergic drugs often cause annoying side effects like dry mouth and blurred vision?

options.A: They block parasympathetic nerve signals throughout the whole body
options.B: They cause a sudden drop in the patient's blood pressure
options.C: They irritate the mucous membranes in the head and neck
options.D: They dehydrate the patient by increasing kidney urine output

explanation: Because these signals help control our body's moisture and secretions, blocking them dries things up everywhere—leading to dry mouth and blurry eyes. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T4#GNS223_U3_T4_h3)

question: What makes providing home health care different from working in a hospital ward?

options.A: There are always doctors present during every shift
options.B: Patients have no say in their daily routines
options.C: Medical equipment is never required in the home
options.D: The nurse operates inside the patient's private residence

explanation: You're stepping into the patient's personal space! Unlike controlled hospital wards, home care means dealing with everyday home environments and variables. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U2_T7#GNS324_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why is teaching patients how to use home blood pressure monitors such an important nursing duty?

options.A: Patients need to know how to solder broken circuit boards at home
options.B: Good technique prevents false readings that could lead to wrong medication changes
options.C: It stops patients from ever coming back to the hospital clinic
options.D: Home machines are so complicated that only rocket scientists can run them

explanation: If a patient uses poor posture or a bad cuff size at home, their doctor might see bad data and change their prescriptions incorrectly. Your teaching makes a real difference! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of a Root Cause Analysis after a serious medical error?

options.A: Finding which specific nurse to terminate immediately
options.B: Writing a public apology letter for the newspaper
options.C: Calculating the financial lawsuit settlement amount
options.D: Discovering the underlying systemic factors that caused the error

explanation: RCA looks beyond the individual worker to examine flawed processes, equipment, and environment factors that permitted the mistake. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h4)

question: When should a nurse apply standard precautions in clinical practice?

options.A: Whenever a patient displays symptoms of an active fever
options.B: Exclusively in intensive care units and surgical theaters
options.C: Only when caring for patients with confirmed airborne diseases
options.D: For all patients receiving care, regardless of their diagnosis

explanation: Standard precautions are the baseline level of infection control used for every single patient interaction to prevent blood and fluid exposure. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h6)

question: Which bioethical principle is about sharing scarce resources fairly during a disaster?

options.A: Veracity
options.B: Justice
options.C: Paternalism
options.D: Autonomy

explanation: Well done! Justice means making sure medical care and resources are distributed fairly without unfair bias during a crisis. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T3#GNS315_U1_T3_h8)

question: Why do we warm up the small mirror before doing an indirect laryngoscopy?

options.A: To clean off germs
options.B: To keep steam from fogging up the mirror
options.C: To numb the back of the throat so they won't gag
options.D: To widen blood vessels in the throat

explanation: Warm patient breath hitting a cold mirror creates fog. Warming the mirror first keeps the reflection clear so you can see the vocal cords. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T2#GNS311_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to healthcare access for youths in Nigeria?

options.A: Financial constraints due to out-of-pocket payments
options.B: Free medical services available at every clinic
options.C: Judgmental attitudes from healthcare providers
options.D: Fear of breaking confidentiality laws or parental rules

explanation: Free medical services are rare, and financial cost is actually one of the biggest barriers young people face in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h4)

question: What happens to staff morale if hospital management uses MBO goals purely as a punitive tool?

options.A: Nurses become significantly more motivated to achieve higher targets
options.B: Patient satisfaction scores rise immediately due to strict rules
options.C: Administrative efficiency increases across all hospital departments
options.D: Staff feel anxious and view the process with fear rather than trust

explanation: Using goals to punish creates a toxic culture where staff hide mistakes instead of collaborating to fix them. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h6)

question: A care assistant is about to feed a resident who has trouble swallowing. What safety tip should you give?

options.A: Offer large chunks of solid food for better chewing
options.B: Feed the resident as quickly as possible
options.C: Position the resident in an upright sitting posture
options.D: Encourage the resident to lie flat on the bed

explanation: Brilliant! Sitting upright uses gravity to help swallowing and keeps food out of the lungs, preventing dangerous choking. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T1#GNS324_U5_T1_h4)
